source: Documented obesity diagnosis rate in primary care: 19.9% (Mayo Clinic cohort, Bardia et al., https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/17673060/) and 18% (2024 International Journal of Obesity study, https://www.nature.com/articles/s41366-024-01514-6). Global default pending per-country curation.

Derived, not directly observed: anti-obesity medication (AOM) fill rate among all US adults was 4.4% (2015-2023, medRxiv/CBO-cited literature) against a ~19% documented-diagnosis base, implying roughly 23% of diagnosed patients are treated. Wide band reflects that this is a ratio of two different studies, not a single cohort measurement. Global default pending per-country curation.

Modelling assumption: share of pharmacologically-treated obesity patients who are candidates for the current GLP-1/GIP-GLP-1 class specifically (as opposed to older agents), reflecting current US prescribing patterns where GLP-1s dominate new anti-obesity starts. Not from a single cited study; global default pending per-country curation.

IDF Diabetes Atlas 2025: 42.8% of adults with diabetes are undiagnosed globally (diagnosed = 57.2%), improving to 28.8% undiagnosed in high-income countries (diagnosed = 71.2%). Value is a blended midpoint since this market set mixes high-income and middle-income countries; low/high span the global-to-high-income range. https://diabetesjournals.org/care/article/49/3/490/164378

Modelling assumption: most diagnosed type 2 diabetes patients are prescribed at least first-line pharmacotherapy (e.g. metformin) per ADA Standards of Care. Not from a single cited study; global default pending per-country curation.

Modelling assumption: share of treated type 2 diabetes patients who are candidates for injectable/GLP-1 add-on therapy under treatment-intensification guidelines, beyond first-line oral monotherapy. Not from a single cited study; global default pending per-country curation.
